header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Time: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Liu (Redwood SE), Ana Gomez (Redwood Solutions), Priya Rao (Cobalt - ML Platform Lead), Tom Hernandez (Cobalt - CTO), Zoe Kim (Cobalt - SRE), Evan Brooks (Cobalt - NLP Engineer)
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing latest quantization sweep. Main findings: FP8 variant keeps quality within threshold for chat prompts but shows occasional hallucination patterns on the 'long-context' set; INT8 yields 18-22% throughput improvement but at cost of 1.5-3% quality delta on entity/slot extraction set. Next steps focus on targeted prompt filtering, KV cache warm-up experiments, and a canary plan. Security docs and parameter sweep CSV to be shared before next week.
topics: Quant sweep results summary (INT8 vs FP8)
Quality delta breakdown by prompt class
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off. Quick roll call — uh — Jordan and Ana from our side.
[00:12] Jordan Liu: Hey all.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Priya here.
[00:18] Tom Hernandez: Tom on my end.
[00:22] Zoe Kim: Zoe — SRE.
[00:25] Evan Brooks: Evan, hi.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda: quick recap of last week's tuning, go through the quant sweep results Jordan ran, then discuss canary and security items.
[00:45] Jordan Liu: I'll share screen — uh — you might see some slides, they're rough. Before that, quick reminder: this sweep was run on the target GPU (A10x-sim) with both INT8 convert path and FP8 blend mode. We included a 50/50 mix of short-chat prompts and long-context doc prompts.
[01:10] Evan Brooks: Quick Q: was the KV cache warm path simulated? Last time we saw big cold-cache p95 jumps.
[01:18] Jordan Liu: Good call. We ran two modes: cold-start (no KV warm) and steady-state cache. Cold start shows p95 latency blow-ups, especially INT8, due to re-compilation-ish hot paths. The runtime logs call it "K V cash" sometimes in the trace — sorry transcription artifact.
[01:36] Tom Hernandez: When you say "INT8 shows blow-ups" what's the magnitude?
[01:40] Jordan Liu: Cold p95 for INT8 was about 1.9x baseline FP32; steady-state p95 for INT8 is about 0.82x baseline, so faster in steady state. FP8 steady-state p95 was 0.9x baseline.
[01:55] Priya Rao: And quality? The business cares about entity extraction on customer churn prompts — that's our top metric.
[02:02] Jordan Liu: Right. We bucketed quality into three: open-chat coherence, slot/NER accuracy (entity), and long-context fidelity (references). INT8 had a 2.6% drop on NER set, FP8 0.9% drop. On long-context, FP8 had occasional hallucinations where it dropped reference scoring by ~4% on the 5% tail.
[02:30] Maya Patel: To be explicit: your SLA we're mapping to is <2% degradation on entity extraction, right?
[02:36] Priya Rao: Yes, ideally under 1.5.
[02:38] Maya Patel: Okay so FP8 is closer but still edge cases.
[02:42] Zoe Kim: Can we do a hybrid: FP8 for long-context and INT8 for short chat? Means routing complexity though.
[02:50] Jordan Liu: We actually tested a blended routing policy — prefix-based routing where longer tokens go FP8, short go INT8. That reduced cost by ~12% while keeping overall entity delta at 1.2%, but it added routing latency of ~6-8ms at the gateway.
[03:08] Tom Hernandez: 6-8ms gateway is okay if p95 stays under 200ms, our user experience bar.
[03:14] Evan Brooks: How deterministic are these deltas? We saw variance across repeats last sprint.
[03:20] Jordan Liu: There's variance; the biggest source is prompt mix and temperature. We re-ran with client-like sampling and variance tightened. We're attaching the CSV with each run seed and prompt tags.
[03:32] Priya Rao: Where can we see the seed and client sampling?
[03:35] Jordan Liu: In the CSV attached to the report — I'll push that to the shared drive; link coming in the notes.
[03:42] Maya Patel: Security question: KMS provider and at-rest key rotation — have you verified compatibility with our HashCorp Vault setup?
[03:49] Ana Gomez: On Redwood Private we've tested with AWS KMS and Vault in staging. The KMS integration should be straightforward, but for Vault our on-prem connector needs a tiny network NAT rule.
[03:58] Zoe Kim: We'll need a network diagram and specific port list.
[04:02] Ana Gomez: Absolutely — we'll send that.
[04:06] Priya Rao: Can you also confirm audit log retention options? We need 2 years for compliance.
[04:10] Maya Patel: Redwood Console supports custom retention for audit logs; can export to S3 for long-term. We'll include retention configs in the security pack.
[04:19] Evan Brooks: Back to perf: do we have cost comparison for blended route vs full FP8?
[04:24] Jordan Liu: Full FP8 reduces cost ~20% vs fp32 at steady-state; INT8 is ~38% lower. Blend sits around ~28% lower overall in our synthetic mix. But that'll vary by prompt length distribution.
[04:40] Tom Hernandez: One of our concerns is regression risk in weekend traffic when we ramp; what's rollback look like?
[04:46] Maya Patel: Canary + automatic fallback to higher precision model on quality regressions. The rollout plan includes a quick abort if entity accuracy drops below your threshold for a 10-minute window.
[04:56] Priya Rao: That sounds good. Can we get an SLA on detection time?
[04:59] Jordan Liu: Detection is near real-time with our eval hooks — roughly within 2 minutes for the configured alerting metrics, depending on sampling.
[05:07] Zoe Kim: Are evaluations run on production prompts or sampled proxies?
[05:11] Jordan Liu: We support both. For privacy you can run on anonymized sample set; we recommend a small shadow stream of real prompts for fastest detection if allowed.
[05:20] Priya Rao: Ok — on the quality front Evan had some notes about examples where FP8 hallucinated references. Evan, can you share quickly?
[05:26] Evan Brooks: Yeah — short summary: in one test the model invented a date that wasn't in doc when context overlapped across chunk boundaries. Seems like quantization caused attenuation of positional cues in some layers.
[05:38] Jordan Liu: We saw that too; hypothesis is a sensitivity in attention scaling in layer 9-11 — when we re-run with slight layer-wise mixed precision (keeping layers 9-11 at fp16) the hallucination disappears in most cases with minor perf impact.
[05:53] Tom Hernandez: So mixed-precision per-layer is on the table. What overhead?
[05:57] Jordan Liu: About 4-6% throughput cost vs full FP8 but quality back within your 1.5% bound in our tests.
[06:06] Priya Rao: That may be our best compromise.
[06:09] Maya Patel: Great. Jordan, can you mark that as the recommended config for the next canary?
[06:13] Jordan Liu: Yep, will include in the sweep export.
[06:16] [10:12] — [this timestamp jump indicates long run of data review slides, some silence and note taking—not all speech captured perfectly]
[16:00] Jordan Liu: Quick note on cold-cache mitigation: we can pre-warm prefix cache for common templates. We saw p95 falls by ~300ms on long-doc flows if warm-up is used.
[16:12] Zoe Kim: Do pre-warms increase memory footprint significantly?
[16:15] Jordan Liu: Depends on headroom, but typically a small percent of KV cache RAM; we can cap by TTL.
[16:22] Priya Rao: Network egress on pre-warm? We don't want big upfront egress cost.
[16:26] Ana Gomez: Pre-warm is internal between nodes; no extra egress billed across cloud provider, just intra-cluster internal traffic.
[16:33] Zoe Kim: Good.
[16:36] Evan Brooks: Anything on tokenizer variance? We saw slight changes when re-tokenizing for quantization pipeline.
[16:41] Jordan Liu: Tokenizer differences accounted for ~0.3% of observed quality delta — smaller than the int8 effect. We recommend freezing tokenization in production to avoid drifts.
[16:51] Tom Hernandez: Ok, practical ask: we want a recommended config that balances cost and entity accuracy <1.5% and p95 <200ms. Can Redwood produce that and maybe two fallback configs?
[17:02] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll deliver 1) recommended (FP8 mixed-layer), 2) cost-opt (blend INT8/FP8 with routing), 3) safe fallback (FP16). Each with rollbacks and expected unit economics.
[17:14] Priya Rao: Perfect. Also legal asked for the subprocessor list and data lifecycle.
[17:19] Maya Patel: We'll include subprocessor list in the security pack.
[17:22] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[17:25] Jordan Liu: One more experiment we ran: ephemeral micro-batching at inference gateway — lowers GPU context switches by grouping sub-10 token prompts for 10ms windows. Net effect: +6% throughput, +2ms latency. Might help short-chat volume.
[17:40] Zoe Kim: Would batching affect real-time chats? We can't add visible lag.
[17:44] Jordan Liu: It's configurable; you set latency floor. We tested with 15ms cap and found UX impact negligible.
[17:51] Tom Hernandez: We'll want a dashboard showing token-level cost and latency by route. Can Redwood surface that?
[17:56] Ana Gomez: Yes, Redwood Console already offers per-route latency and token cost. We'll show a sample dashboard in the follow-up.
[18:04] Priya Rao: Ok, timeline recap? We need to finalize pilot config by mid-Jan.
[18:09] Maya Patel: Let's make milestones: security pack by 12/31, parameter sweep CSV by 01/05, internal bench by 01/06, canary plan 01/07, canary start 01/12. Does that work?
[18:21] Tom Hernandez: That fits our Q1 runway.
[18:24] Priya Rao: Action items noted.
[18:28] Maya Patel: Any other risks we haven't covered?
[18:31] Zoe Kim: Egress costs when moving to dedicated cluster in EU — need cost estimates per TB.
[18:36] Maya Patel: We'll include egress per TB estimates for each deployment mode.
[18:40] Evan Brooks: One last technical: is there an easy knob to pin KV eviction? We saw some churn.
[18:45] Jordan Liu: TTL and pinned prefix options exist; we'll recommend tuning params in the runbook.
[18:50] Priya Rao: Great.
[18:53] Maya Patel: Ok, wrap. Quick recap of next steps — we covered that in the notes. Thanks everyone.
[18:59] Tom Hernandez: Thanks.
[19:02] Priya Rao: Thanks all.
[19:05] [End of meeting — notes: link to the CSV and security pack to be uploaded to shared drive; full sweep attachments will include seed IDs and prompt tags; meeting recording saved. Some transcription artifacts present.]
